skill.description: Use Bandit to scan Python projects for common security vulnerabilities, map findings to OWASP and CWE categories, and plan secure remediation.
skill.summary: Guides Python security scanning with Bandit, CWE and OWASP mapping, CI gates, and remediation guidance.
skill.author: AgentSecOps

security_audit.summary: Reviewed all 150 static detections in context. Nearly all are false positives from Markdown formatting, Bandit configuration data, public dependency references, or explicitly labeled vulnerable examples in remediation docs. One changed-file xargs pipeline remains a medium-confidence operational risk because unusual repository filenames can affect command invocation.

remediation.issue: Changed-file scan command uses xargs without robust filename handling.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the pipeline with a NUL-delimited workflow, add an option separator before file paths, or use a small wrapper that validates Python paths before invoking Bandit.

content.user_title: Scan Python Code with Bandit SAST
content.value_statement: Python teams need fast security checks before code reaches CI. This skill guides Bandit scans, pre-commit setup, OWASP and CWE mapping, and remediation.
actual_capabilities: Explains Bandit installation, recursive scans, severity filters, and report generation.
Provides a baseline Bandit configuration with common exclusions and threshold guidance.
Maps Bandit finding families to CWE and OWASP Top 10 categories.
Gives remediation guidance for secrets, SQL injection, command injection, weak cryptography, and deserialization.
Includes a pre-commit configuration for Bandit and related Python security checks.
limitations: The referenced scripts/bandit_analyzer.py file is not present in this skill package.
Bandit focuses on Python code and does not find every business logic flaw.
Users must install and trust Bandit, pre-commit, and any selected hook repositories.
Bandit reports can include sensitive snippets unless users suppress code output.

use_cases.title: Review Python Pull Requests
use_cases.description: Run Bandit before merge and triage new findings by severity, confidence, CWE, and OWASP category.

use_cases.title: Fix Vulnerable Python Patterns
use_cases.description: Use the remediation guide to replace unsafe SQL, subprocess, cryptography, and deserialization patterns.

use_cases.title: Add CI Security Gates
use_cases.description: Configure Bandit in pre-commit or CI so medium and high severity findings block risky changes.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Basic Scan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner scan of a Python project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me run Bandit against this Python project and explain the severity and confidence levels in plain language.

prompt_templates.title: Triage Findings
prompt_templates.scenario: Review a Bandit report after a scan.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Bandit findings, group them by priority, and identify which issues should block the release.

prompt_templates.title: Map to Compliance
prompt_templates.prompt: Map these Bandit issue IDs to CWE and OWASP Top 10 categories, then summarize the compliance impact.

prompt_templates.title: Design a CI Gate
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Bandit pre-commit and CI policy for a legacy Python service with gradual enforcement and documented exceptions.

output_examples.input: A Bandit report contains hardcoded password and subprocess shell findings.
output: High priority: remove hardcoded credentials and rotate any exposed secrets.
High priority: replace shell command construction with argument lists and input validation.
Track each fix with CWE and OWASP references for review evidence.

output_examples.input: A team wants Bandit in pre-commit without blocking all legacy issues.
output: Start with warnings for the full baseline.
Block new high severity findings first.
Raise enforcement after owners document accepted exceptions.

output_examples.input: A developer asks how to remediate unsafe deserialization.
output_examples.output: Avoid pickle for untrusted data. Prefer JSON or MessagePack with schema validation, and document any trusted internal exception.

best_practices: Run Bandit in CI with clear severity and confidence thresholds.
Store Bandit reports carefully because snippets can expose secrets.
Document each suppression with a specific security justification.
anti_patterns: Do not treat all low confidence findings as safe without review.
Do not copy vulnerable examples from remediation guides into production code.
Do not bypass pre-commit or CI security gates without documented approval.

faq.question: Does this skill run Bandit by itself?
faq.answer: No. It guides the user or agent through Bandit commands and configuration choices.

faq.question: Which languages does Bandit scan?
faq.answer: Bandit scans Python source code. Other languages need separate SAST tools.

faq.question: Can it map findings to OWASP and CWE?
faq.answer: Yes. The included reference maps common Bandit test IDs to CWE and OWASP Top 10 categories.

faq.question: Can it be used in pre-commit?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes a pre-commit configuration that can run Bandit before commits.

faq.question: Are Bandit findings always true vulnerabilities?
faq.answer: No. Findings need review because Bandit can report false positives and context-dependent issues.

faq.question: What should users protect during scans?
faq.answer: Protect reports, logs, and artifacts because they may contain source snippets or secret values.
